title: Greg Isenberg's startup ideas: action apps, loneliness, AI native media, niche selection
summary: Greg Isenberg and Jonathan Courtney each pick favorite startup categories: agent-first action apps, loneliness and community businesses, elder tech, AI employees, vertical health, pet health and AI native media. Greg's recurring lessons are to pick an underserved niche with disposable income, verticalize, and build where incumbents are slow to move.

principles.text: Reinvent apps as agent-first: apps that do things for you, not apps you stare at.
principles.quote: apps that do things for me, not apps I stare at and that rely on human beings, what can I reinvent in mobile such that uh you know, I'm a first mover advantage.

principles.text: Incumbents struggle to go agent-first, just as Facebook struggled with mobile, which opens a window for new builders.
principles.quote: it's going to be hard for companies to basically do the transition to become agent-first. And I think that's the opportunity for people listening right now.

principles.text: Users want convenience to the max, so don't worry that full automation hurts engagement.
principles.quote: people just want convenience to the max.

principles.text: Sell AI employees by picking the vertical and job title, then listing jobs to be done and adding them over time.
principles.quote: pick the vertical and pick the job title and then go and think about all the jobs to be done for that particular job title.

principles.text: Loneliness is a large, real opportunity; recurring memberships fit community and event businesses.
principles.quote: a membership model makes sense. Um so, you know, I I'd encourage people to look at memberships. Um and the beauty about that is you're getting recurring revenue.

principles.text: Pick a niche that is underserved, has disposable income, and a big pain point; the product can change.
principles.quote: I do think that they should go and pick a niche that they one think is underserved, two think has disposable income, and three has a big pain point.
